title: Patellar Tracking

positions.as_written: Expect instability to present near extension and pain to present in flexion, because the restraints differ there.
Assess the extensor mechanism through movement, since a static axial view misses the engagement arc entirely.
Treat a poorly reproducible clinical sign as a prompt for imaging rather than as a measurement.
Identify which part of the arc fails before choosing between a soft tissue and a bony procedure.
Read a J sign as late or lateral engagement rather than as a quadriceps problem.
Prefer a dynamic study where the static indices and the history disagree.
State that the flexion angle of engagement is not routinely measured, rather than implying an index captures it.
Expect a soft tissue reconstruction to work inside the window and to do little outside it.
